sentences.text:
The brief facts of the prosecution case are as follows:
The accused Nos.1 and 2 are married couple, at the instance and instructions of her husband / accused No.2 Smt. Kavitha @ Rani / accused No.1 on 22.09.2013 at about 9.30 a.m. came to the house of Smt. Prathibha Kulakarni situated at No.70, 9 th Main, Nobonagar, Bannerghatta Road within the limits of Hulimavu police station seeking household work, since complainant was also in need of a maid, she took her as a maid servant, thereafter accused No.1 under the pretext of cooking food added stupefying substance in the milk, administered the same to CW.1, she lost her consciousness and regained the same at around 2.00 p.m., when she regained the consciousness, she found missing of 2 layered one gold chain with coral and a gold ring, 3 pairs of ear studs and a mobile.

being police officials of Hulimavu police station, having learnt the fact that accused Nos.1 to 3 are under the pretext of seeking employment of household works in the residential houses are in the habit of committing theft by administering sleeping pills or stupefying substance / drugs without bringing the same to the notice of their officers went to the house of accused No.1 situated at Anekal and to the house of accused Nos.2 and 3 situated at Marathahally in Maruti Omni car in a civil dress,
projected themselves as police officials in front of accused Nos.1 to 3, extorted the gold jewels and other stolen articles from accused Nos.1 to 3 by threatening them and accused Nos.4 to 6 unlawfully seized those jewels or stolen articles, distributed among themselves.

Thereafter, on 17.10.2013 the accused No.1 to 3 were apprehended by CW.10 and on investigation found the commission of theft in the house of CW.1 by administering sleeping pills in the food and making her to sleep without consciousness.

4. On the basis of complaint lodged by CW.1 Smt. Prathibha Kulkarni, Hulimavu Police have registered this case in Cr.No.611/2013 against accused No.1 to 6 for the offences punishable u/s 328,
420, 411 and 201 IPC.

Thereafter, investigation officer visited the spot and drawn spot mahazar, also recovered the stolen 2 layered gold chain with coral in the house of accused Nos.2 and 3 through seizure mahazar in the presence of witnesses and subjected the same under P.F. No.140/2013, also seized rings and ear rings in the house of accused Nos.1 and 2 through seizure mahazar in the presence of CW.1 and CW.2 and subjected the same under P.F. No.141/2023 for the offences punishable u/s 328, 420, 411 and 201 of IPC.

After conducting arrest procedure accused Nos.1 to 6,
they were produced before the jurisdictional court.
Silver item stolen by accused No.1 in the house of CW.1 was recovered and seized from accused No.5 through seizure mahazar in the presence of witnesses and subjected the same under P.F. No.133/2015.

I.O. recorded the statements of CW.1 as Hulimavu Ps vs A1-Kavitha Alias Rani on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199198858/
3 well as mahazar witnesses, recorded voluntary statement of accused and based on the voluntary statement of accused seizure mahazars as stated supra have been drawn.

sentences.text: After completion of investigation, being of the opinion that there is prima-facie case against accused No.1 to 6 submitted final report.

5. Cognizance for the offences shown in the charge sheet was taken against accused Nos.1 to 6 by the learned Magistrate, thereafter a criminal case against accused persons was registered in C.C.
No.30468/2015 on the file of V ACMM, Bengaluru, since offences alleged against accused persons are exclusively triable by the court of sessions, the same was committed to this court.
6. After committal, the case is registered as S.C. No.347/2018.
Prosecution opened the case as required u/s 226 of Cr.P.C.

Heard learned counsel for the accused, no grounds made out to discharge the accused, hence, charge against accused Nos.1 to 6 for the offences punishable u/s 328,
420, 411 and 201 of IPC was framed, its contents were read over and explained, they denied the charges and claimed to be tried.

7. To prove the ingredients of the offences leveled against the accused Nos.1 to 6, prosecution in all cited 18 witnesses, among them 11 witnesses were examined as PW.1 to PW.11 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and got identified 2 material objects from MO.1 and MO.2.

CW.6,
CW.8 and CW.9 are not secured in spite of giving sufficient opportunity, hence they have been dropped.
CW.5 is reported as dead.

The learned public prosecutor given up the evidence of CW.13,
CW.14 and CW.17 as not required in order to avoid repetition, thereby closed its side evidence.

8. After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statement of accused Nos.1 to 6 u/s 313 of Cr.P.C.
has been recorded and they have denied all the incriminating material evidence appearing against them and not chosen to lead their side defence evidence.
9.
Heard arguments on both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

10. The points that arise for my determination are:
1) Whether prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on 22.09.2013 at being married couple with an intention of committing theft in order to have wrongful gain accused No.2 insisted and instructed his wife accused No.1 to join the house of CW.1 situated at No.17, 9 th Main Road, Nobonagar, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru as maid servant, accordingly accused No.1 approached CW.1 Smt. Prathibha Kulkarni requested to take her to the household work, since CW.1 was also in need of a maid servant joined her for the said work, as such accused No.1 under the pretext of doing household work added sleeping pills or stupefying substance while preparing food to the CW.1, administered the same, when CW.1 lost her consciousness, as per the instructions of accused No.2 and layered gold chain with coral, finger rings, 3 pairs of ear rings and a mobile phone, when CW.1 regained her consciousness, she found the missing of aforesaid gold ornaments and mobile phone, thereby accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable u/s 328 r/w 34 of IPC?

sentences.text:
It is the specific case of the prosecution that, accused Nos.1 to 3 were involved in the commission of theft with a plan of joining a house for house keeping and thereafter by administering sleeping pills or stupefying substance in the food of the respective owners commit the theft of valuables such as gold, silver including cash.
13.

In this connection, prosecution in order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons has examined 11 witnesses out of 18 witnesses, among them complainant is examined as PW.5, her husband is examined as PW.6, seizure mahazar witnesses one Chowri Rajnu and Somashekhar are examined as PW.1 and PW.8.
Police officials who apprehended accused persons are examined as PW.3, PW.4, PW.7 and PW.9.
I.Os. Are examined at PW.10 and PW.11.
The prosecution has also relied on 18 documents.

The complaint is marked at Ex.P.5, seizure mahazars are at Exs.P.1, P.3 and P.15, FIR is at Ex.P.8, spot mahazar is at Ex.P.6, voluntary statements of accused can be seen at Exs.P.11 to P.13, P.17 and P.18.

The prosecution has also relied on 2 material objects as MO.1 and MO.2.
14.
As per the contents of complaint which is marked at Ex.P.5 alleged incident has taken place on 22.09.2013 and the complaint is lodged on 20.10.2013 i.e., after 28 days of the alleged incident.

The complainant Smt. Prathibha Kulakarni examined as PW.5 and in her evidence it is deposed that on 22.09.2013 one Rani aged about 20 to 22 years had come to her house under the pretext of seeking household work and she pleaded her inability to feed milk to her child due to poverty, therefore she joined her home to do the household work, she prepared dosa to her husband, thereafter her husband went out of the house, the said Rani prepared tea for her, after having tea she got drowsiness, thereafter she lost her conscious, she got up at 2 O' clock when her husband rang up the calling bell, by that time the said worker Rani was not at home, her mobile was missing along with her valuables such as 2 layered gold chain with coral, 2 pairs of gold ear rings, one gold finger ring,
one small ear stud and since she was going to her place due to urgent work, she could not lodge the complaint.
15. It is further stated that this PW.5 came to know about modus-operandi for commission of theft in the news papers as well as in the TV.
Therefore, she lodged complaint before the Hulimavu police station as per Ex.P.5.

Thereafter, the police have visited the place of incident and conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P.6 in her presence and after 2 years of the incident Hulimavu police had called her showed some of the stolen articles, among them, she got her 2 layered gold chain with coral, one pair of ear stud, silver bowls, she identified the said gold articles as MO.1 and MO.2.

Further, in her cross-examination upon seeing accused Nos.1, 2 and 5 this witness has failed to identify the accused No.1 who was present in the court hall, even she failed to identify accused Nos.2 and 3.

As per the prosecution, accused Nos.2 and 3 had joined the accused No.1 to the household work in the house of complainant, this witness was subjected to cross- examination by the prosecution, she denied the suggestion of prosecution that she is deposing falsely in order to help the accused person.

In her cross- examination she narrates about the incident and also says that before taking any maid servants to the house, she will inquire about their antecedents or background, their antecedents will Hulimavu Ps vs A1-Kavitha Alias Rani on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199198858/
6 be seen and it takes 4 - 5 days to get familiar with the things which have kept in the kitchen to use it for cooking work.

sentences.text: Further in cross- examination she has stated that normally she will lock cupboard and she does not have the receipt for having purchased the articles, it can be seen from the cross- examination of this witness that she has admitted about lodging of complaint at the belated stage.

16. Further, the learned counsel on behalf of the accused No.6 tried to elicit improvements in the version of complainant, she has admitted that after taking accused No.1 as maid worker, she prepared dosa to them, she woke up only when her husband had rang up the calling bell at 2.00 p.m. and these things stated in the chief examination have not been mentioned in the complaint, she has admitted the fact that after 28 days of the incident there was a T.V. telecast with respect to alleged theft involved in this case, as such by watching T.V. she lodged the complaint against the accused Nos.1 to 3 and even this fact was also not mentioned in the complaint.
It is stated by this witness that, she was advised to lodge complaint about the theft in her house when she had been to police station.

It is further pleaded by the complainant that when she visited the police station gold ornaments were kept on the table and she was made to identify her ornaments and further she failed to state what are the ornaments kept on the table and denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that there was no theft as alleged in the complaint.
17.
PW.1 Chouri Raju is a seizure mahazar witness in respect of recovery of gold and silver articles as per Ex.P.1.
According to this witness he signed on Ex.P.1 in the Hulimavu police station, he pleaded his ignorance about the contents of Ex.P.5 and thereby not supported the case of the prosecution.

He was subjected to cross-examination as he turned hostile, he denied the suggestion of the prosecution that he was present at the time of recovery of one 2 layered gold chain with coral, one silver bowl, nothing substantial was elicited from the cross-examination of this witness.
18. Another witness Srinivas. N., is examined as PW.2, he is also seizure mahazar witness as per Ex.P.3.
he has completely turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution, he saying that police have obtained his signature on blank papers and pleaded his ignorance about contents of Ex.P.3.

Prosecution subjected him for cross-examination by treating him as hostile, he denied the suggestion of the prosecution that he was present during recovery of 2 layered gold chain with coral,
mobile phone, credit cards, Reliance mutual fund etc.
19.

Another seizure witness Somashekharappa is examined as PW.8, he has not supported the case of prosecution he denies entire process of seizure mahazar, though, prosecution treated him as hostile, nothing substantial is elicited in his cross-examination, he denied entire suggestion of the prosecution.

20. PW.6 - Sharath Kulakarni is the husband of complainant, he has spoken regarding conducting of spot mahazar in his presence at his home, he identified the signature at Ex.P.6, he has admitted that he do not know the contents of Ex.P.6.
21.
In the cross-examination he admits that he cannot remember the contents of spot mahazar and denies the suggestion that he signed the said mahazar in the police station.

sentences.text: PW.3 Jagadeesh is a police official, who has deposed regarding securing accused No.6 as per the order of Police Inspector CW.11 Rajesh Kotia, identified the accused No.6 before the court.
In the cross- examination he denies the suggestion of the defence counsel that he has not apprehended the accused No.6 as stated in his chief examination.

23. Another witness PW.4 Smt. Savitha Bai is also a police official, who has deposed regarding securing of accused No.1 along with her colleagues CW.12 Chandrappa, CW.13 Chandru and CW.14 Nagesh near Koli Farm gate, Weavers Colony, she identified accused No.1 who was present before the court, she denied the suggestion of defence counsel that she was not at all deputed to apprehend accused No.1.

24. PW.7 - B.K. Nageshaiah has deposed regarding registration of FIR on the basis of the complaint lodged by PW.5, conducting of spot mahazar as per Ex.P.6 in the presence of CW.2 - Sharath Kulkarni, husband of the complaint.

He has further deposed about conducting of arrest procedure on accused Nos.1 to 3, recording of their voluntary statements and also handed over accused Nos.1 to 3 for conducting further investigation to the custody of CW.10.
He identified the accused Nos.1 to 3 and stated that after completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against accused persons.

25. In the cross-examination on behalf of the accused Nos.1 to 3 this witness denies a suggestion that Ex.P.5 complaint was prepared in the police station and also denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that they have created the complaint as well as FIR as per the instructions of their higher officials without there being any recovery.
It is admitted by this witness that he has not chosen any local persons as mahazar witnesses.
Further, PW.7 has denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that person who registered the FIR is not supposed to file the final report.

26. In the cross-examination of PW.7 on behalf of the accused Nos.4 to 6, I.O. has admitted the registration of Cr.No.591/2013 and arrest of accused in the said case much prior to the registration of this case.

This I.O. admits that he has not subjected the complainant for any medical examination nor conducted spot mahazar in the place where allegedly dosa and tea were prepared and also not furnished the bill and receipt for having purchased the gold ornaments.

27. In the cross-examination of I.O. it can be seen that accused in their voluntary statements have not stated that they have committed theft in the house of CW.1 and they have added stupefying substance in the tea and at the same time it is further stated by this witness that accused stated about commission of theft in the Nobonagar area.
Further, this witness has denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that he has not recorded the voluntary statements of the accused in the Cr.No.611/2013 and recorded only in 591/2013.
28. PW.9 is also police official, he has deposed regarding apprehending of accused No.1 along with PW.4 - Smt. Savitha Bai, he identified accused Nos.1 to 3 before the court.

In his cross-examination he has stated that there was no written order by his higher officer about deputing him for patrolling duty on the alleged date of incident and denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that he has not at all deputed for apprehending of accused person.

sentences.text: PW.10 is the then Assistant Commissioner of Police of CCB, he has stated that he was appointed to conduct further investigation in this matter with regard to accused Nos.4 to 6.

In his chief examination he has deposed regarding earlier investigation conducted by PW.7 - B.K. Nageshaiah and further investigation conducted by himself, he has further deposed regarding drawing up of seizure mahazar, subjecting the recovered articles in P.F. Nos.132/2013 and 133/2013.

This witness deposed regarding recording of statements of police officials, also conducting of seizure mahazar in the presence of witnesses as per Ex.P.12, recording of voluntary statements of accused Nos.4 to 6 and recovery of articles involved in the case, drawing up of mahazar as per Ex.P.15, he recorded the statements of accused Nos.1 to 3 in respect of identification of accused Nos.4 to 6 by them, thus this witness elaborately stated about the investigation.
30. It is admitted by this witness that before taking up the investigation, voluntary statements of accused Nos.1 to 3 were recorded by CW.7 Nagaiah.

In the cross-examination of defence counsel,
they have attempted to point out the latches in the investigation such as non-mentioning denomination of cash seized under mahazar, non-mentioning of laptops, bills and documents as to say the ownership of such laptops, denies the suggestion of the defence counsel that he has not conducted any seizure mahazar as per Exs.P.1, P.3 and P.15 and also denies the suggestion of the defence counsel that they have falsely implicated police officials in this case with an intention of causing harassment.
31. PW.11 Rajesh Kotia has deposed regarding arrest of accused Nos.4 to 6 along with seizure of Samsung, Appel and Nokia mobile phones.
Thus, this witness denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that he has not conducted any investigation, not recorded statement of accused and so on.

32. From over all consideration of evidence of each witnesses and also on perusal of exhibits, it is evident that the complainant has lodged the complaint after 28 days of the incident on a reason that the complainant had urgent work so that she could not lodge the complaint well in time.

However, it can be noticed from the oral evidence of this witness, that she has lodged complaint only when there was a paper publication as well as T.V. telecast regarding the commission of theft along with alleged modus operandi employed for commission of such theft, this witness also states that she has lodged complaint at the instance of police when she visited the police station after incident of 28 days.

33. Though, the complainant is examined as PW.5 she narrates incident regarding commission of alleged offence of theft in her house, she failed to identify the accused No.1 who allegedly joined her house through accused Nos.2 and 3 for the work of house keeping and under the pretext of preparing food she added stupefying substance or sleeping pills in the tea which was allegedly consumed by the complainant, resulted in drowsiness and fall asleep, as a result she committed theft of gold and silver articles as well as Nokia mobile phone of the complainant.

Though, the prosecution partly treated her as hostile and suggested that the accused No.1 who was before the court was the same lady who had come to her house on 22.09.2013 seeking house keeping work and after joining added the stupefying substance in her tea, this complainant has failed to identify her,
which is a serious blow on the case of the prosecution, husband of the complainant is only a spot mahazar witness, he pleaded his ignorance about the contents of mahazar which is not helpful to the case of the prosecution.

9 34.

Insofar as recovery of gold articles allegedly stolen by the accused No.3 in the house of CW.1 is concerned, it is not supported by any independent seizure mahazar witnesses who were examined as PW.1, PW.2 and PW.6.
The official witnesses have spoken regarding apprehending of accused Nos.1 to 6 since the seizure mahazar witnesses have turned hostile.

The allegations of the prosecution that,
after commission of theft by accused Nos.1 to 3, other accused No.4 to 6 having learnt about the theft of gold articles as well as mobile phone, visited the house of accused Nos.1 to 3, recovered all such stolen articles from them without informing the same to their higher officers, distributed among themselves and kept in their possession has not been established to bring home the guilt that the accused Nos.4 to 6 by deceiving recovered stolen articles possessed the same with them in order to have unlawful gain.
35. In addition, there are no incriminating material evidences against accused Nos.4 to 6 insofar as the allegation of screening of evidence u/s 201 of IPC.

Thus, non establishment of recovery of seizure of the stolen articles through the independent seizure mahazar witnesses became the fatal to the case of the prosecution to bring home the guilt of the accused.

None of the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution, the person who sets the criminal law into motion failed to identify the prime accused allegedly involved in the commission of offence.
Under the circumstances, evidence of I.O. in respect of investigation remains formal and not established with the corroborative evidence of independent witnesses.
Under such circumstances, the oral evidence of I.O. is not sufficient to prove the seizure of material objects and seizure of beyond reasonable doubt.
It is the I.O. who has deposed only in support of prosecution case.

36. It is true that the police officials have supported the case of prosecution by deposing about apprehending of accused persons and their evidence cannot directly be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused as the evidence of police official is not supported by the seizure mahazar witnesses and their evidence is confined to investigation duties, as such it can be said that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt with cogent, convincing and corroborative evidence.
Hence, points No.1 to 4 are answered in the Negative.
37. POINT NO.5:

In view of the above finding on points No.1 to 4, this court is of the opinion that,
the evidence on record is grossly insufficient to prove the guilt of the accused Nos.1 to 6 for the aforementioned offences.
Hence, they are entitled for acquittal.

Accordingly, this court proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
Invoking provision u/s 235(1) of Cr.P.C., accused Nos.1 to 6 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable u/s 328, 420, 411 and 201 r/w Sec. 34 of I.P.C.
The bail bonds of accused Nos.1 to 6 and their sureties bonds stand cancelled.
Bail bond executed by accused Nos.1 to 6 u/s 437-A of Cr.P.C., shall be in force for a period of six months from this day.
The order of interim custody of MO.1 - two layers gold chain with coral and MO.2 - ear stud seized under P.F. Nos.140/2013 and 141/2013 are made absolute.

being police officials of Hulimavu police station, having learnt the fact that accused Nos.1 to 3 are under the pretext of seeking employment of household works in the residential houses are in the habit of committing theft by administering sleeping pills or stupefying substance / drugs without bringing the same to the notice of their officers went to the house of accused No.1 situated at Anekal and to the house of accused Nos.2 and 3 situated at Marathahally in Maruti Omni car in a civil dress,
projected themselves as police officials in front of accused Nos.1 to 3, extorted the gold jewels and other stolen articles from accused Nos.1 to 3 by threatening them and accused Nos.4 to 6 unlawfully seized those jewels or stolen articles, distributed among themselves.

opennyai_summary.issue:
10. The points that arise for my determination are:
1) Whether prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on 22.09.2013 at being married couple with an intention of committing theft in order to have wrongful gain accused No.2 insisted and instructed his wife accused No.1 to join the house of CW.1 situated at No.17, 9 th Main Road, Nobonagar, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru as maid servant, accordingly accused No.1 approached CW.1 Smt. Prathibha Kulkarni requested to take her to the household work, since CW.1 was also in need of a maid servant joined her for the said work, as such accused No.1 under the pretext of doing household work added sleeping pills or stupefying substance while preparing food to the CW.1, administered the same, when CW.1 lost her consciousness, as per the instructions of accused No.2 and layered gold chain with coral, finger rings, 3 pairs of ear rings and a mobile phone, when CW.1 regained her consciousness, she found the missing of aforesaid gold ornaments and mobile phone, thereby accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable u/s 328 r/w 34 of IPC?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Insofar as recovery of gold articles allegedly stolen by the accused No.3 in the house of CW.1 is concerned, it is not supported by any independent seizure mahazar witnesses who were examined as PW.1, PW.2 and PW.6.
The allegations of the prosecution that,
after commission of theft by accused Nos.1 to 3, other accused No.4 to 6 having learnt about the theft of gold articles as well as mobile phone, visited the house of accused Nos.1 to 3, recovered all such stolen articles from them without informing the same to their higher officers, distributed among themselves and kept in their possession has not been established to bring home the guilt that the accused Nos.4 to 6 by deceiving recovered stolen articles possessed the same with them in order to have unlawful gain.
35. In addition, there are no incriminating material evidences against accused Nos.4 to 6 insofar as the allegation of screening of evidence u/s 201 of IPC.
Thus, non establishment of recovery of seizure of the stolen articles through the independent seizure mahazar witnesses became the fatal to the case of the prosecution to bring home the guilt of the accused.
None of the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution, the person who sets the criminal law into motion failed to identify the prime accused allegedly involved in the commission of offence.
Under the circumstances, evidence of I.O. in respect of investigation remains formal and not established with the corroborative evidence of independent witnesses.
Under such circumstances, the oral evidence of I.O. is not sufficient to prove the seizure of material objects and seizure of beyond reasonable doubt.
It is the I.O. who has deposed only in support of prosecution case.
36. It is true that the police officials have supported the case of prosecution by deposing about apprehending of accused persons and their evidence cannot directly be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused as the evidence of police official is not supported by the seizure mahazar witnesses and their evidence is confined to investigation duties, as such it can be said that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt with cogent, convincing and corroborative evidence.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, they are entitled for acquittal.
Accordingly, this court proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
Invoking provision u/s 235(1) of Cr.P.C., accused Nos.1 to 6 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable u/s 328, 420, 411 and 201 r/w Sec. 34 of I.P.C.
The bail bonds of accused Nos.1 to 6 and their sureties bonds stand cancelled.
Bail bond executed by accused Nos.1 to 6 u/s 437-A of Cr.P.C., shall be in force for a period of six months from this day.
The order of interim custody of MO.1 - two layers gold chain with coral and MO.2 - ear stud seized under P.F. Nos.140/2013 and 141/2013 are made absolute.
